'''Isaac B. Bersuker''' (Russian: Исаáк Бóрухович (Бори́сович) Берсýкер; born February 12, 1928) is a Romanian-born [[Soviet Union|Soviet]]-[[Moldova]]n-American theoretical physicist and quantum chemist whose principal research is in [[chemical physics]], [[solid-state physics]], and [[theoretical chemistry]]. Known for his "life-long years of experience in theoretical chemistry"<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Lever|first=A. B. P.|date=1999-05-01|title=Electronic Structure and Properties of Transition Metal Compounds: Introduction to the Theory By Isaac B. Bersuker (The University of Texas at Austin). John Wiley: New York. 1996. ISBN 0-471-13079-6.|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=121|issue=18|page=4544|doi=10.1021/ja975564q|issn=0002-7863}}</ref> working on the [[electronic structure]] and properties of [[Coordination complex|coordination compounds]], Isaac B. Bersuker is "one of the most widely recognized authorities"<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Kaplan|first=Michael D.|date=2006-08-01|title=The Jahn−Teller Effect By Isaac B. Bersuker (University of Texas at Austin). Cambridge University Press: Cambridge. 2006. xvi + 616 pp. $185.00. ISBN 0-521-82212-2.|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=128|issue=32|pages=10631–10632|doi=10.1021/ja069734n|issn=0002-7863}}</ref> in the theory of the [[Jahn–Teller effect]] (JTE) and the [[pseudo Jahn–Teller effect|pseudo-Jahn–Teller effect]] (PJTE). His accomplishments include explaining the polarization of the atomic core in [[Rydberg atom]]s, the effect of [[Quantum tunneling|tunneling]] splitting in molecules and solids with a strong JTE, and the discovery of the PJTE origin of [[ferroelectricity]] in cubic [[perovskite]]s. For many years, known as the leading expert in JTE and PJTE, Bersuker has served as the permanent chairman of the international steering committee of the Jahn–Teller symposia.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Fullerene Theory - University of Nottingham|url=https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/~ppzjld/JTsymposia.htm|access-date=2021-12-23|website=www.nottingham.ac.uk}}</ref> His present affiliation is with the [[Oden Institute for Computational Engineering and Sciences|Oden Institute for Computational Engineering and Science of the Department of Chemistry]] of [[the University of Texas at Austin]]. According to Google Scholar,<ref name=":15">{{Cite web |title=Bersuker I. B. |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=maHGAPQAAAAJ&hl=en&oi=sra |access-date=November 16, 2025 |website=Google Scholar}}</ref> he published 493 titles, including books, review articles, regular articles, and short communications.

==Early life, education, and career==
Isaac (Izya) Bersuker was born on February 12, 1928, in [[Chișinău]], then part of [[Greater Romania]], to a low-income family of [[History of the Jews in Bessarabia|Bessarabian Jewish]] descent. His father Boruch Bersuker was a carpenter, and his mother Bella Bersuker (Russian: Бéлла Хáймовна Берсýкер, 1896–1981) was a housewife with five kids. As a boy in a family of a modest background, Isaac got his elementary school education in [[Talmud Torah]] and [[World ORT|ORT]].  He was 13 years old when the tragic events of [[World War II]] forced his Jewish family to run from the Nazis to an [[Azerbaijan Soviet Socialist Republic|Azerbaijan]] village.<ref name=":0" /> Deprived of the traditional middle and high-school education, he spent four years farming in [[Azerbaijan Soviet Socialist Republic|Azerbaijan]] [[kolkhoz]].<ref name=":11" /> After the war, native Romanian, he barely spoke Russian. Yet, in a self-education way, in а two-year term, he managed to complete a four-year high-school program in a Russian school and [[Matriculation examination|enrolled]] at [[Moldova State University|Chișinău State University]].<ref name=":11" /><ref name=":0">{{Cite book|last1=Borshch|first1=Serguei|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=eMnfAAAACAAJ|title=Advances in Quantum Chemistry. Manifestations of Vibronic Coupling in Chemistry and Physics|last2=Polinger|first2=Victor|publisher=Elsevier Ltd.|year=2003|isbn=978-0-12-034844-2|editor1-last=Ceulemans|editor-first1=Arnout|volume=44|location=San Diego, CA|pages=xxxiii-xxxv|chapter=Anniversary Isaac Bersuker 75|doi=10.1016/S0065-3276(03)44048-3|editor2-last=Chibotaru|editor2-first=Liviu|editor3-last=Kryachko|editor3-first=Eugene|display-editors=1}}</ref> A fascinating autobiographical section in <ref name=":11">{{cite book|title=The Jahn–Teller Effect and Beyond. Selected works of Isaac Bersuker with Commentaries|publisher=The Acad. of Sciences of Moldova and The University of Texas at Austin|year=2008|isbn=978-9975-62-212-7|editor1-last=Boggs|editor1-first=James E.|location=Chișinău, Moldova|publication-date=December 17, 2008|pages=10–31|editor2-last=Polinger|editor2-first=Victor Z.}}</ref> describes "his scientific ascent, starting from a Jewish childhood in Bessarabia and frequently hampered by antisemitic state directives under the [[Stalin and antisemitism|Stalin]] regime."<ref name=":12" /> Dedicated to the study of [[theoretical physics]], in 1952, Bersuker graduated from the university with a master's degree in physics. He began his scientific research in [[atomic spectroscopy]] as a post-graduate student at [[Saint Petersburg State University|Leningrad State University]], working under [[Mikhail Veselov]]<ref>{{Cite web|last=Veselov|first=M. G.|title=Division of Quantum Mechanics|url=https://fock.phys.spbu.ru/english/veselov_en.htm|access-date=2021-12-23|website=fock.phys.spbu.ru}}</ref> at the Division of Quantum Mechanics<ref>{{Cite web|title=Division of Quantum Mechanics|url=https://fock.phys.spbu.ru/english/index_en.htm|access-date=2021-12-23|website=fock.phys.spbu.ru}}</ref> led by its Chair [[Vladimir Fock|Vladimir A. Fock]]. Here, in 1957, Bersuker received his [[Candidate of Sciences]] degree and in 1964 his [[Doctor of Sciences]] degree. From 1964 to 1993, back in Chișinău, Bersuker continued his scientific research at the Institute of Chemistry<ref>{{Cite web|title=Home {{!}} Institute of Chemistry|url=https://ichem.md/en/|access-date=2021-12-23|website=ichem.md}}</ref> of the [[Academy of Sciences of Moldova|Moldavian branch of the USSR Academy of Sciences]]. In 1964, he founded the Laboratory of Quantum Chemistry<ref>{{Cite web|title=Laboratory Physical and Quantum Chemistry {{!}} Institute of Chemistry|url=https://www.ichem.md/en/laboratory-physical-and-quantum-chemistry|access-date=2021-12-23|website=www.ichem.md|language=en}}</ref> also dubbed ''the Chișinău school of the Jahn–Teller effect.''<ref name=":12">{{Cite journal|last=Englman|first=Robert|date=2009-04-01|title=Book Review|journal=Structural Chemistry|language=en|volume=20|issue=2|pages=351–353|doi=10.1007/s11224-009-9438-8|s2cid=195068521|issn=1572-9001}}</ref>  Elected as a Corresponding Member of this academy in 1972 and a full Member<ref>{{Cite web|title=Academia de Științe a Moldovei|url=https://www.asm.md/en/membru?id=7|access-date=2021-12-23|website=www.asm.md}}</ref> in 1989, Bersuker moved to the United States. In 1993, he became a senior research scientist and professor of the department of chemistry<ref>{{Cite web|title=Department of Chemistry, University of Texas at Austin|url=https://cm.utexas.edu/|access-date=2021-12-23|website=cm.utexas.edu}}</ref> at the [[University of Texas at Austin]]. Bersuker served as a doctoral and [[habilitation]] supervisor for 31 post-graduate students and post-docs. According to [[K. Alex Müller]], Bersuker was and still is "in full swing at the university, writing books, discussing with great wit, and quick to understand".<ref>{{Cite book|last=Müller|first=K. Alex|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=eMnfAAAACAAJ|title=Advances in Quantum Chemistry. Manifestations of Vibronic Coupling in Chemistry and Physics.|publisher=Elsevier Science|year=2003|isbn=0-12-034844-6|editor-last=Ceulemans|editor-first=Arnout|volume=44|location=San Diego, CA|pages=xxxv-xxxvi|chapter=Encounters with Isaac Bersuker|author-link=K. Alex Müller|editor-last2=Kryachko|editor-first2=Eugene|editor-last3=Sabin|editor-first3=John R.|editor-last4=Chibotaru|editor-first4=Liviu|display-editors=1}}</ref> In the late 1980s, owing to Bersuker's high motivating role, leadership, and creative ingenuity, Bersuker's school was called "the capital of the Jahn–Teller effect" by some.<ref name=":0" />

==Research==

===Atomic spectroscopy===
In his Ph.D. thesis, Bersuker developed the theory of core [[Polarization density|polarization]] and its effect on [[Transition radiation|optical transitions]] in [[Rydberg atom]]s.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Bersuker|first1=I. B.|date=1957-03-01|title=On the total summation rule for oscillator strengths of alkali metals|trans-title=|journal=Soviet Phys. (Doklady)|language=|volume=2|issue=|pages=167–169|issn=0038-5689|oclc=1023153322|osti=4331475|via=ISBN 978-9975-62-212-7, pp.57-59}}</ref> At the time, this was a puzzling problem in [[absorption spectroscopy]]. The absorption of light by [[Alkali metal|alkali atoms]] appeared to violate the [[Electric dipole transition|electric dipole]] [[Sum rule in quantum mechanics|sum rule]]. According to Bersuker, the solution to the problem is in the instantaneous polarization of the [[atomic core]] by the incident electromagnetic wave creating an additional [[Perturbation theory (quantum mechanics)|perturbation]] to the excitation of the [[valence electron]]. Related to this problem, he worked out the [[Adiabatic theorem|adiabatic separation of motion]] of the valence and the [[atomic core]] electrons in [[electronic structure]] calculations of atoms.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Veselov|first1=M. G.|last2=Bersuker|first2=I. B.|year=1958|title=Adiabatic approximation in quantum theory of atoms.|url=|journal=Izvestija Akademii Nauk SSSR|series=Ser. Fizicheskaia|language=Russian|volume=22|issue=6|pages=662–663|bibcode=1958IzSSR..22..662V}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Veselov|first1=M. G.|last2=Bersuker|first2=I. B.|year=1962|title=Calculation of the lithium atom in the adiabatic approximation and computation of its nuclear magnetic moment|journal=Opt. Spectr. (USSR) (English Transl.)|language=|volume=13|issue=3|pages=167–169|bibcode=1962OptSp..13..167V|issn=0030-4034|osti=4719250}}</ref> First introduced in 1957, still, decades later, Bersuker's ideas of electron polarization by the incident electromagnetic wave and of the atomic core polarization by the valence electron is used and further explored in atomic spectroscopy.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Hansen|first1=Jørgen E.|last2=Laughlin|first2=Cecil|last3=Hart|first3=Hugo W. van der|last4=Verbockhaven|first4=Gilles|date=1999|title=Energy levels, wavefunction compositions and electric dipole transitions in neutral Ca|journal=Journal of Physics B: Atomic, Molecular and Optical Physics|language=en|volume=32|issue=9|pages=2099–2137|doi=10.1088/0953-4075/32/9/305|bibcode=1999JPhB...32.2099H|s2cid=250830221 |issn=0953-4075}}</ref>

===Jahn–Teller and pseudo Jahn–Teller effects===
Bersuker's contributions to the JTE and PJTE theory with applications to physical and chemical phenomena are reflected in his several monographs (some of them written and published with the assistance and involvement of other authors) and major reviews on this subject (see the latest in<ref name="book1">{{cite book |last1=Bersuker |first1=Isaac B. |title=The Jahn–Teller Effect |date=2006 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |location=Cambridge, UK |doi=10.1017/CBO9780511524769 |isbn=978-0-521-82212-1 }}</ref><ref name="book2">{{Cite book|last1=Bersuker|first1=Isaac B.|url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007%2F978-3-642-83479-0|title=Vibronic Interactions in Molecules and Crystals|last2=Polinger|first2=Victor Z.|publisher=Springer-Verlag|year=1989|isbn=978-3-540-19259-6|series=Springer Series in Chemical Physics|volume=49|location=Berlin, Heidelberg|doi=10.1007/978-3-642-83479-0|hdl=10821/3407|issn=0172-6218}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|last=Bersuker|first=Isaac B.|date=2021|title=Jahn–Teller and Pseudo-Jahn–Teller Effects: From Particular Features to General Tools in Exploring Molecular and Solid State Properties|journal=Chemical Reviews|volume=121|issue=3|pages=1463–1512|doi=10.1021/acs.chemrev.0c00718|pmid=33353296|s2cid=229690173|issn=0009-2665}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite book|last=Bersuker|first=Isaac B.|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/book/10.1002/9781119165156|title=Advances in Chemical Physics|publisher=John Wiley & Sons, Inc.|year=2016|isbn=978-1-119-16515-6|editor-last=Rice|editor-first=Stuart A.|volume=160|pages=159–208|chapter=Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking in Matter Induced by Degeneracies and Pseudodegeneracies|doi=10.1002/9781119165156.ch3|issn=1934-4791|editor-last2=Dinner|editor-first2=Aaron R.}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite journal|last=Bersuker|first=I. B.|date=2017|title=The Jahn–Teller and pseudo Jahn–Teller effect in materials science|journal=Journal of Physics: Conference Series|language=en|volume=833|issue=1|article-number=012001|doi=10.1088/1742-6596/833/1/012001|bibcode=2017JPhCS.833a2001B|s2cid=136171872 |issn=1742-6596|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Bersuker|first=Isaac B.|date=2013-03-13|title=Pseudo-Jahn–Teller Effect—A Two-State Paradigm in Formation, Deformation, and Transformation of Molecular Systems and Solids|journal=Chemical Reviews|volume=113|issue=3|pages=1351–1390|doi=10.1021/cr300279n|pmid=23301718|issn=0009-2665}}</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite journal|last=Bersuker|first=I. B.|date=2018-11-18|title=Vibronic (pseudo Jahn–Teller) theory of ferroelectricity: Novel aspects and applications|journal=[[Ferroelectrics (journal)|Ferroelectrics]]|volume=536|issue=1|pages=1–59|doi=10.1080/00150193.2018.1528919|bibcode=2018Fer...536....1B |s2cid=126940116|issn=0015-0193}}</ref>). First published in 1961–1962, his contributions to the theory of the JTE predicted the tunneling splitting of the vibronic energy levels of the systems with the JTE,<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Bersuker|first=I. B.|date=1963|title=Inversion splitting of levels in free complexes of transition metals|url=https://jetp.ras.ru/cgi-bin/dn/e_016_04_0933.pdf|journal=Soviet Physics JETP|language=|volume=16|issue=4|pages=933–938|bibcode=1963JETP...16..933B|issn=0038-5646|oclc=1128379287}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Bersuker|first1=I. B.|last2=Vekhter|first2=B. J.|last3=Ogurtsov|first3=I. Ya.|date=1975|title=Tunnel effects in polyatomic systems with electronic degeneracy and pseudodegeneracy.|url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1070/PU1975v018n08ABEH004913/pdf|journal=Sov. Phys. Usp.|language=|volume=18|issue=8|pages=569–587|doi=10.1070/PU1975v018n08ABEH004913|issn=0038-5670|oclc=960772943|url-access=subscription}}</ref> later confirmed experimentally. The splitting is due to the [[Quantum tunnelling#Related phenomena|tunneling]] transitions between the equivalent wells on the multiminimum adiabatic potential energy surface produced by this effect. In 1976, "The phenomenon of tunneling splitting of energy levels of polyatomic systems in the state of electronic degeneracy" was qualified as a scientific discovery and registered in the State Register of the USSR (Diploma No. 202).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Discovery: The phenomenon of tunneling splitting of energy levels of polyatomic systems in the state of electronic degeneracy (Author: Academician, Professor Isaac Bersuker) |url=https://www.asm.md/en/discovery-phenomenon-tunneling-splitting-energy-levels-polyatomic-systems-state-electronic}}</ref> In addition, Bersuker is known for revealing the significance of the PJTE and showing that it may take place at any energy gaps between entangled electronic states. Most important, he proved that ''the JTE and PJTE are the only sources of structural instability and spontaneous symmetry breaking'' (SSB) in polyatomic systems.<ref name="book1" /><ref name="book2" /><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Bersuker|first1=Isaac B.|last2=Gorinchoi|first2=Natalia N.|last3=Polinger|first3=Victor Z.|date=1984-05-01|title=On the origin of dynamic instability of molecular systems|journal=Theoretica Chimica Acta|language=en|volume=66|issue=3|pages=161–172|doi=10.1007/BF00549666|s2cid=98728524|issn=1432-2234}}</ref> Thus, according to Bersuker, if a polyatomic system has broken symmetry properties, undoubtedly, they are of JTE or PJTE origin. This conclusion elevates the two effects from their assumed earlier rare particular features to general tools for exploring molecular and solid-state properties.<ref name="book1" /><ref name="book2" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite book|last=Bersuker|first=I. B.|title=Electronic structure and properties of transition metal compounds: introduction to the theory|date=2010|publisher=Wiley|isbn=978-0-470-57305-1|edition=Second|location=Hoboken, N.J.|oclc=632158142}}</ref><ref name=":3" /><ref name=":4" />

The generality of this result was challenged by the existence of some molecular systems with SSB. For example, in the ozone O<sub>3</sub> molecule, neither the JTE nor the PJTE is seen explicitly in the high-symmetry configuration. Bersuker eliminated this controversy by revealing the ''hidden'' JTE and PJTE.<ref>{{Citation|last=Bersuker|first=Isaac B.|chapter=Recent Developments in the Jahn–Teller Effect Theory: The Hidden Jahn–Teller Effect |date=2009|title=The Jahn–Teller Effect: Fundamentals and Implications for Physics and Chemistry|pages=3–23|editor-last=Köppel|editor-first=Horst|series=Springer Series in Chemical Physics|volume=97|place=Berlin, Heidelberg|publisher=Springer|language=en|doi=10.1007/978-3-642-03432-9_1|isbn=978-3-642-03432-9|editor2-last=Yarkony|editor2-first=David R.|editor3-last=Barentzen|editor3-first=Heinz}}</ref> They take place in the excited states of the system but, being strong enough, penetrate the ground state of the high-symmetry configuration and form an additional, coexisting equilibrium state with lower symmetry. The latter may also have a different spin state leading to an interesting phenomenon of [[Spin crossover|''spin-crossover'']] ''and magnetic-dielectric bistability.''<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Bersuker|first=Isaac B.|date=2020|title=Spin Crossover and Magnetic-Dielectric Bistability Induced by Hidden Pseudo-Jahn–Teller Effect|journal=Magnetochemistry|language=en|volume=6|issue=4|page=64|doi=10.3390/magnetochemistry6040064|doi-access=free}}</ref> Involving excited states, Bersuker also showed that the PJTE is instrumental in explaining the origin of chemical activation and sudden polarization in photochemical reactions.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=BERSUKER|first=I. B.|date=1980|title=Are activated complexes of chemical reactions experimentally observable ones?|url=|journal=Nouv. J. Chim.|publisher=Cambridge: Royal Society of Chemistry|volume=4|issue=3|pages=139–145|issn=0398-9836|id=https://pascal-francis.inist.fr/vibad/index.php?action=getRecordDetail&idt=PASCAL8060250194}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Wang|first1=Ya|last2=Liu|first2=Yang|last3=Bersuker|first3=Isaac B.|date=2019-05-22|title=Sudden polarization and zwitterion formation as a pseudo-Jahn–Teller effect: a new insight into the photochemistry of alkenes|url=https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlelanding/2019/cp/c9cp01023h|journal=Physical Chemistry Chemical Physics|language=en|volume=21|issue=20|pages=10677–10692|doi=10.1039/C9CP01023H|pmid=31086864 |bibcode=2019PCCP...2110677W|s2cid=149779106|issn=1463-9084|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Revealed by Bersuker, other applications of the JTE and PJTE are briefly mentioned below.

==Solid-state problems: ferroelectricity and multiferroicity==
Another fundamental contribution of Isaac B. Bersuker to the early developments of this field was applying the PJTE to explain the origin of [[ferroelectricity]] in [[perovskite]]-type crystals.<ref name=":14">{{Cite journal|last=Bersuker|first=I. B.|date=1966-04-01|title=On the origin of ferroelectricity in perovskite-type crystals|journal=Physics Letters|language=en|volume=20|issue=6|pages=589–590|doi=10.1016/0031-9163(66)91127-9|bibcode=1966PhL....20..589B|issn=0031-9163}}</ref> This first application of the PJTE to solve an important solid-state problem led to developing a whole trend in the studies of local and cooperative properties in crystals. The origin of crystals' temperature-controlled spontaneous [[Dielectric#Dielectric polarization|dielectric polarization]] was the subject of discussion for many decades involving high-rank physicists at the time. However, with the development of the experimental technics, the "displacive theories" encountered increasing controversies that had no explanation.

Using perovskite crystals as an example, Bersuker showed (first in 1964, published in 1966<ref name=":14" />) that the PJTE produces a spontaneous symmetry breaking resulting under certain conditions in local dipolar instability. It exists in all the crystal phases, and the spontaneous polarization results from the order-disorder interaction between these PJTE-induced local dipolar distortions. Performed in the local octahedral TiO<sub>6</sub> center in the [[Barium titanate|BaTiO<sub>3</sub>]] crystal (taken as an example), where vibronic coupling mixes ground <sup>1</sup>''A''<sub>1g</sub> and close in energy exited <sup>1</sup>''T''<sub>1u</sub> states of opposite parity (but same multiplicity), detailed analysis with calculations proved the PJTE to produce the dipolar distortion. Thus, it shows that Bersuker's PJTE theory of ferroelectricity agrees with the available empirical data and predicts new properties,<ref name=":4" /><ref name=":7">{{Cite journal|last1=Bersuker|first1=Isaac B.|last2=Polinger|first2=Victor|date=2020|title=Perovskite Crystals: Unique Pseudo-Jahn–Teller Origin of Ferroelectricity, Multiferroicity, Permittivity, Flexoelectricity, and Polar Nanoregions|journal=Condensed Matter|language=en|volume=5|issue=4|page=68|doi=10.3390/condmat5040068|doi-access=free|bibcode=2020CondM...5...68B }}</ref> confirmed experimentally.

From the fact that PJTE does not entangle states with different [[Spin (physics)#Spin projection quantum number and multiplicity|spin multiplicity]], Bersuker deduced conditions and predicted possible [[multiferroics]] in some cubic perovskites.<ref name=":6">{{Cite journal|last1=Garcia-Fernandez|first1=Pablo|last2=Bersuker|first2=Isaac B.|date=2011-06-17|title=Class of Molecular and Solid State Systems with Correlated Magnetic and Dielectric Bistabilities Induced by the Pseudo Jahn–Teller Effect|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.106.246406|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=106|issue=24|article-number=246406|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.106.246406|pmid=21770587|bibcode=2011PhRvL.106x6406G|hdl=10902/26489 |hdl-access=free}}</ref>  According to Bersuker, only the ''d''<sup>n</sup> cations with the close-energy ground and excited states of opposite parity, but with the same multiplicity, may meet the necessary conditions of ferroelectricity in the presence of unpaired spins.<ref name=":6" />

==Novel solid-state property: orientational polarization==
Under external unipolar perturbations, polar gases and liquids manifest two kinds of [[Dielectric#Dielectric polarization|polarization]], displacive and orientational. The latter is by orders of magnitude larger than the former. So far, solids were known to undergo only displacive polarization. Bersuker showed that in ABO<sub>3</sub> type perovskites, dipolar distortions are due to the PJTE.<ref name=":5">{{Cite journal|last1=Bersuker|first1=I.B.|date=1966-04-01|title=On the origin of ferroelectricity in perovskite-type crystals|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/0031916366911279|journal=Physics Letters|language=en|volume=20|issue=6|pages=589–590|bibcode=1966PhL....20..589B|doi=10.1016/0031-9163(66)91127-9|issn=0031-9163|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref name=":7" /><ref name=":8">{{Cite journal|last=Bersuker|first=I. B.|date=2015-01-12|title=Pseudo Jahn–Teller effect in the origin of enhanced flexoelectricity|url=https://aip.scitation.org/doi/10.1063/1.4905679|journal=Applied Physics Letters|volume=106|issue=2|page=022903|doi=10.1063/1.4905679|bibcode=2015ApPhL.106b2903B|hdl=2152/31050|s2cid=119788341 |issn=0003-6951|hdl-access=free}}</ref><ref name=":9">{{Cite journal|last=Bersuker|first=Isaac B.|date=2015-11-16|title=Giant permittivity and electrostriction induced by dynamic Jahn–Teller and pseudo Jahn–Teller effects|url=https://aip.scitation.org/doi/10.1063/1.4936190|journal=Applied Physics Letters|volume=107|issue=20|page=202904|doi=10.1063/1.4936190|bibcode=2015ApPhL.107t2904B|issn=0003-6951|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Similar to the other cases of the JTE and PJTE,<ref name=":14" /> the adiabatic potential energy surface of the metallic B center has eight equivalent wells positioned along the eight diagonals of the cube, meaning eight symmetry-equivalent positions of the PJTE-induced dipole moment with small barriers between them. As a result, these dipoles can rotate under external perturbations realizing orientational polarization.<ref name=":8" /><ref name=":9" /> Predicted more than a century ago by [[Peter Debye|P. Debye]], solids with intrinsic dipoles behave like polar liquids with orientational polarization. However, enhanced [[polarizability]] of such solids was not well understood until Bersuker's works<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":5" /><ref name=":8" /><ref name=":9" /> (see also in<ref name=":4" /><ref name=":7" />). As shown by Bersuker, experimentally observed giant flexoelectricity, permittivity, and electrostriction result from PJTE-induced orientational polarization.<ref name=":4" /><ref name=":7" /><ref name=":8" /><ref name=":9" />

==Molecular puckering (buckling) and its suppression==
Given that the PJTE is the unique source of structural instability, Bersuker applied this idea to planar configurations of some molecules in nondegenerate states. Bersuker was the first to demonstrate that the puckering (or buckling) of planar two-dimensional systems is of PJTE origin.<ref name="book1" /><ref name="book2" /><ref name=":1" /> Hence, following Bersuker, their planarity can be driven by external influence targeting the PJTE parameters.<ref name=":10">{{Cite journal|last=Bersuker|first=I. B.|date=2017|title=Manipulation of structure and properties of two-dimensional systems employing the pseudo Jahn–Teller effect|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S2452262717301174|journal=FlatChem|language=en|volume=6|pages=11–27|doi=10.1016/j.flatc.2017.10.001|issn=2452-2627|url-access=subscription}}</ref> As the starting example, he suggested hemoglobin oxygenation. The out-of-plane displacement of the iron atom was shown to be due to the PJTE. At the same time, the coordination of the oxygen atom violates the condition of the PJTE instability, thus restoring the planar configuration.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Bersuker|first1=I. B.|last2=Stavrov|first2=S. S.|date=1988|title=Structure and properties of metalloporphyrins and hemoproteins: the vibronic approach|journal=Coordination Chemistry Reviews|language=en|volume=88|pages=1–68|doi=10.1016/0010-8545(88)80001-8|issn=0010-8545|doi-access=free}}</ref> In a more general setup, such manipulations became more critical recently because of the applications of two-dimensional molecular systems in electronics. According to Bersuker, planarity can be operated by targeted redox perturbations, coordination with other atomic groups, and chemical substitutions.<ref name=":10" /> A similar modification of a crystal lattice by redox influencing its local JTE centers was also realized.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Gudkov|first1=V. V.|last2=Sarychev|first2=M. N.|last3=Zherlitsyn|first3=S.|last4=Zhevstovskikh|first4=I. V.|last5=Averkiev|first5=N. S.|last6=Vinnik|first6=D. A.|last7=Gudkova|first7=S. A.|last8=Niewa|first8=R.|last9=Dressel|first9=M.|last10=Alyabyeva|first10=L. N.|last11=Gorshunov|first11=B. P.|date=2020|title=Sub-lattice of Jahn–Teller centers in hexaferrite crystal|journal=Scientific Reports|language=en|volume=10|issue=1|page=7076|doi=10.1038/s41598-020-63915-7|doi-access=free|issn=2045-2322|pmc=7184747|pmid=32341430|bibcode=2020NatSR..10.7076G}}</ref>

==Other problems==
There is quite a list of other [[theoretical chemistry]], [[chemical physics]], and [[quantum chemistry]] fields with a remarkable Bersuker's contribution. In a number of his seminal papers, Bersuker introduced and developed theoretical models of vibronic mechanisms in [[redox]] properties, electron-conformational effects,<ref>{{Cite book|last=Bersuker|first=Isaac B.|title=Electronic Structure and Properties of Transition Metal Compounds: Introduction to the Theory|work=Chapter 10.|publisher=John Wiley & Sons, Inc.|year=2010|isbn=978-0-470-18023-5|edition=2-nd|location=Hoboken, NJ|pages=579–622|chapter=Electron Transfer, Redox Properties, and Electron-Conformational Effects}}</ref> chemical [[Reactivity (chemistry)|reactivity]], and [[catalysis]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Bersuker|first=I. B.|title=The Jahn–Teller Effect and Vibronic Interactions in Modern Chemistry.|work=Chapter 6|publisher=Plenum Press|year=1984|isbn=978-0-306-41319-3|location=New York|pages=251–290|chapter=Activation Mechanisms in Chemical Reactions and Catalysis}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Bersuker|first=Isaac B.|title=Electronic Structure and Properties of Transition Metal Compounds: Introduction to the Theory.|work=Chapter 11.|publisher=John Wiley & Sons, Inc.|year=2010|isbn=978-0-470-18023-5|edition=2-nd|location=Hoboken, NJ|pages=623–691|chapter=Reactivity and Catalytic Action.}}</ref> He is known for revealing the role of JTE and PJTE in the properties of [[Mixed-valence complex|mixed-valence compounds]].<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Bersuker|first1=I. B|last2=Borshch|first2=S. A.|date=1992|title=Vibronic interactions in polynuclear mixed-valence clusters|url=https://pascal-francis.inist.fr/vibad/index.php?action=getRecordDetail&idt=5479212|journal=Adv. Chem. Phys.|series=Advances in Chemical Physics |volume=81|pages=703–782|doi=10.1002/9780470141380.ch6 |isbn=978-0-471-54570-5 |issn=0065-2385|url-access=subscription}}</ref> In addition, he discovered the effect of [[Coordination covalent bonds|coordination covalent]] [[Bonding (chemistry)|bonding]] and the JTE in the "plasticity effect".<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Gazo|first1=J.|last2=Bersuker|first2=I. B.|last3=Garaj|first3=J.|last4=Kabesova|first4=M.|last5=Kohout|first5=J.|last6=Langfelderova|first6=H.|last7=Melnik|first7=M.|last8=Serator|first8=M.|last9=Valach|first9=F.|date=1976|title=Plasticity of the coordination sphere of copper(II) complexes, its manifestation and causes|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0010854500803173|journal=Coordination Chemistry Reviews|language=en|volume=19|issue=3|pages=253–297|doi=10.1016/S0010-8545(00)80317-3|issn=0010-8545|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Also, Bersuker worked out a [[QM/MM|quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics]] method of [[electronic structure]] calculations of large [[Organometallic chemistry|organometallic]] systems when there is [[Charge-transfer complex|charge transfer]] between the QM and MM parts.<ref>{{Citation|last=Bersuker|first=Isaac B.|title=Computational Chemistry: Reviews of Current Trends|chapter=Methods of Combined Quantum/Classical (QM/MM) Modeling for Large Organometallic and Metallobiochemical Systems|date=2001-08-01|chapter-url=https://www.worldscientific.com/doi/abs/10.1142/9789812799937_0003|volume=6|pages=69–135|publisher=WORLD SCIENTIFIC|doi=10.1142/9789812799937_0003|isbn=978-981-02-4660-0|access-date=2021-09-20}}</ref> The name of Bersuker is associated with the [[Semi-empirical quantum chemistry method|semiempirical]] approach to [[Relativistic quantum chemistry|relativistic electronic structure calculations]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Bersuker|first1=I. B.|last2=Budnikov|first2=S. S.|last3=Leizerov|first3=B. == Personal life ==
Isaac B. Bersuker was married in 1951 to Liliya Bersuker (Russian: Ли́лия [[Russian patronymic|Бори́совна]] Берсýкер, 1930–2003), a chemist. He has one son, Gennadi I. Bersuker<ref>{{Cite web|last=Bersuker|first=Gennadi I.|title=Scopus preview - Bersuker, Gernnadi I. - Author details - Scopus|url=https://www.scopus.com/authid/detail.uri?authorId=7004345214|access-date=2021-12-23|website=www.scopus.com}}</ref> (born 1953), a theoretical physicist, and two grandsons, Eugene G. Bersuker (born 1979) and Kirill G. Bersuker<ref>{{Cite web|last=Bersuker|first=Kirill G.|title=Calico Life Sciences|url=https://www.linkedin.com/in/kirill-bersuker-1033232b/}}</ref> (born 1985), a molecular biologist.
